subject: food-technology
title: Food Provenance & Sustainability: Foundations
welcome_lead: Find out where your food really comes from and what that costs the planet.
meta_desc: GCSE foundations of food provenance: food miles, seasonality, organic, labels.
final_note: Provenance is the story behind every meal you eat.

concepts.def: Where a food was grown, reared or made.
Distance food travels from source to plate.

Scheme paying farmers a guaranteed fair price.
UK quality and welfare assurance label.

walkthroughs.body_html: Provenance describes the origin of a food — where it was grown, how it was reared, who made it. Labels like "British beef" or "Cornish cheese" are claims about provenance, and many shoppers now choose based on them.

Food miles are the distance food travels before being eaten. Air-freighted produce racks up huge miles and emissions. Buying seasonal UK food cuts miles, supports local farmers and often tastes better.

UK shoppers see many trust labels. Organic bans artificial pesticides. Fair Trade guarantees a fair price for growers in developing countries. Red Tractor shows UK-produced food meeting welfare and food-safety standards.
